title: Qatar, Switzerland, and Seventy Thousand Empty Seats in Silicon Valley. The World Cup Comes to the Bay Area.
excerpt: Saturday's Group B match at Levi's Stadium puts the biggest sporting event on earth in the backyard of one of America's largest Indian communities.
body:
The FIFA World Cup arrives in the San Francisco Bay Area on Saturday when Qatar take on Switzerland at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara — and for the hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans who call the region home, it marks a once-in-a-generation moment in their own backyard.

## One Stadium, Two Continents, Three Million NRIs

The Bay Area is home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the United States. Santa Clara County alone has an Indian-origin population exceeding 200,000, with the broader region — stretching from Fremont to Sunnyvale to San Jose — forming the densest concentration of NRIs anywhere outside the Indian subcontinent.

For a community that has largely experienced global football through early-morning television streams from Europe and late-night broadcasts from South America, Saturday's match at Levi's Stadium is something altogether different. The World Cup is no longer an event that happens in distant time zones. It is happening on the 101 freeway.

## The Match: More Than a Group B Fixture

On paper, Qatar versus Switzerland is a Group B contest between a reigning Asian champion trying to prove itself on the biggest stage and a solid European side expected to progress. Qatar, ranked 42nd in the world, endured a difficult home World Cup in 2022, losing all three group matches and failing to score a single goal. They arrive in North America with a point to prove.

Switzerland, ranked 19th, are a different proposition entirely. Semifinalists at Euro 2024, Murat Yakin's side combines the defensive discipline of Yann Sommer's goalkeeping with the creative brilliance of Granit Xhaka and Xherdan Shaqiri.

The match kicks off at 12 PM Pacific Time — a rare afternoon start that puts it squarely in the weekend plans of Bay Area families. For NRIs used to setting 4 AM alarms for Champions League finals, this is a luxury.

## Getting There: An NRI's Guide to Levi's Stadium

Levi's Stadium, home to the San Francisco 49ers, seats over 68,000 and sits adjacent to the Great America theme park in Santa Clara. For Bay Area residents, reaching the stadium is straightforward — Caltrain runs a match-day shuttle service from the Santa Clara station, and VTA light rail stops directly at the Great America Transit Center.

Parking fills up fast, and at $60 and above for match-day spots, public transit is the smarter play. NRIs driving in from Fremont, Cupertino, or San Jose should budget at least 90 minutes for traffic and parking logistics.

## What Else Is on Saturday

Saturday's World Cup card is stacked. After the Santa Clara kickoff, Brazil face Morocco at New York New Jersey Stadium (3 PM PT), followed by Haiti versus Scotland in Boston (6 PM PT) and Australia versus Turkey in Vancouver (9 PM PT). For those planning a full day of football, the Bay Area's dozens of cricket-and-football pubs — from Qs Billiard Club in San Jose to British Bankers Club in Menlo Park — will be screening every match.

## The Bigger Picture

The World Cup will return to the Bay Area later in the tournament. Group J's Austria versus Jordan is scheduled for Levi's Stadium on June 16, and the venue is set to host knockout-stage matches in early July. For NRIs who secure tickets to Saturday's opener, it could be the first of several World Cup nights in Silicon Valley.

India may not be playing in this World Cup, but the Indian community in the Bay Area does not need a national team on the pitch to show up. From the packed viewing parties during IPL season to the sold-out Diljit Dosanjh concerts at the same stadium, this is a community that turns out. Saturday, they get to turn out for the biggest sporting event on earth — right at home.
